subject: DPA variants & subprocessor bridge plan — approval for fallback routing
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Ryan <emma.ryan@medicorp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA variants & subprocessor bridge plan — proposal for fallback routing

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, MediCorp wants a single-signer DPA but also needs concrete operational fallback protections if a primary region or subprocessor becomes unavailable. To move quickly we prepared two deliverables:

- Redlined DPA Variant (ATTACHED: redwood-dpa-variant-v2.pdf) — two lightweight edits that address your onshore-residency ask and incident reporting SLA.
- Subprocessor Bridge Matrix (ATTACHED: subprocessor-bridge-matrix.xlsx) — a mapping of primary -> fallback providers, and what technical compensating controls (onshore caching, HSM key segregation, audit-pulls) we will apply per fallback.

Key asks from our side to finish negotiation:
1) Confirm which fallback model you prefer: "onshore cache + HSM escrow" vs "multi-region active-active with encrypted KV failover" (we recommend the former for predictable forensics).
2) If MediCorp requires explicit UK IDTA / addendum language for UK residents, tell us which boilerplate you prefer (we can supply either SCCs + UK Addendum OR a combined DTIAs template).
3) Approval to route the final DPA to legal for a single-executive signature and then to procurement for the PO cadence.

I flagged Kimberly and Marissa to keep the subprocessor matrix accurate and to lock down evidence items for your TIAs/DTIAs questions. If you want a short 30-min follow-up tomorrow to run the matrix live, we can do that.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147

Attachment: redwood-dpa-variant-v2.pdf (PDF, 42KB)
Attachment: subprocessor-bridge-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 78KB)

From: Emma Ryan <emma.ryan@medicorp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medicorp.com
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: DPA variants & subprocessor bridge plan — proposal for fallback routing

Ben —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the two artifacts. High-level thoughts:

- The "onshore cache + HSM escrow" option is preferred operationally for MediCorp because it gives us a clear audit trail and faster evidence pulls for regulators.
- We will need explicit language about subprocessor notification windows (we generally ask 30 days, but may accept 15 for critical patches).
- For UK subjects: we need the UK IDTA addendum with paragraph referencing our national redress (we'll attach our legal note).

Can you and your team prep a short appendix that maps the subprocessor matrix rows to specific evidence (SOC2 report dates, access logs retention, KMS audit events) so our privacy team can pre-seed the TIA review? Procurement is OK to accept single-signer DPA but wants clear escalation steps if the fallback is invoked.

If you can get that appendix and a 1-page executive summary, procurement will greenlight the PO sequence.

Best,
Emma Ryan
VP Legal, MediCorp
emma.ryan@medicorp.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Ryan <emma.ryan@medicorp.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 08 Aug 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA variants & subprocessor bridge plan — proposal for fallback routing

Emma / Ben / Marissa —

I reviewed the redline and sketched a short appendix that ties matrix entries to evidence buckets. High-level notes below; appendix draft is in Drive (see link).

- Subprocessor notifications: we can commit to 30-day advance notice for non-critical additions and 15-day notice for security-critical swaps. We'll add explicit language for emergency swaps with immediate notice + post-event report within 72 hours.
- UK IDTA: we'll include the UK Addendum template and a targeted recital that references UK transfer safeguards; that will be a 1-paragraph insertion rather than a full separate schedule to avoid divergence.
- Fallback invocation: suggest the following step sequence (we should add to the DPA as an operational exhibit):
  1) Automated alert + triage (internal).
  2) Localized onshore cache activation (if configured).
  3) KMS key rotation and escrow-witness log; customer has right to request snapshot.
  4) Joint forensic window (30 days) with agreed evidence pull scope.

I also attached a short checklist of exact evidence types we'll provide per fallback (SOC2 type II, KMS audit trail, access review logs, dated subprocessor contract).

Ben — if procurement needs a single-page exec summary, I can draft one for legal sign-off. Marissa — can you confirm we can generate the 72-hour post-event report and give an ETA on the evidence pull templates?

On the DocuSign side, I can produce the final combined DPA + exhibit and route to Emma as soon as Marissa confirms the evidence buckets.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
